gamespot.com/articles/activision-keeps-s.title: Activision Keeps Saying All The Right Things About Modern Warfare 4
gamespot.com/articles/activision-keeps-s.excerpt: Activision has made a key announcement about how Double XP tokens work in the upcoming Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and it sounds like good news. Beginning with MW4, 2XP tokens will only count down when you're actually in a match. Previously, the timer would tick down when you were in a game's menus or searching for a match. That's not ideal for a lot of reasons, obviously. https://twitter.com/CallofDuty/status/2104619925881168010 If you're anything like me, sometimes you have to get up to let your dog out. Or you want to get up to grab some food or a drink. Or, you might sit in the game's menus when nature calls. Now, you can do those things and still get the full amount of 2XP without your bonus going to waste. Beyond this, several key developers at Infinity Ward discussed a range of hot topics about MW4 in a newly published "The Road to Launch" video. Check it out below to hear what the team had to say about time-to-kill values, spawning algorithms, and UI issues following the game's multiple rounds of beta testing. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AG68xO8uuq4 This is just the latest positive-sounding update for MW4, following the previous confirmation that players will be able to toggle off skins they don't want to see in Warzone --though the toggle is not supported for MW4 itself yet. Modern Warfare 4 launches on October 23 for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and PC. The game marks the first Call of Duty release on a Nintendo platform since 2013's Call of Duty: Ghosts. It's also the first game since Ghosts to skip PS4 and Xbox One.

gamespot.com/articles/wow-forevers-beta-.title: WoW: Forever’s Beta Just Keeps Getting Bigger
gamespot.com/articles/wow-forevers-beta-.excerpt: World of Warcraft: Forever's beta is in full swing, and if its popularity is any indication of how the full launch might go, it's going to be big, as Blizzard has had to increase the beta's population cap multiple times. Forever was Blizzard's big finale during its BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony , a modified version of WoW Classic that keeps the old-school MMORPG's gameplay and world but brings plenty of new changes and content as well. It's something WoW Classic players have asked for years, and Blizzard is now finally ready to deliver. The beta kicked off September 17 with an initial level cap of 20 and will run through October 21, with Forever's full launch slated for November 4. It's important to note that it's not an open beta that anyone can join. Players need to purchase the $60 Skyborne Epic Pack (which unlocks the new playable Skyborne race in Forever) to gain access . https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=buBZRiQXl8U&t=1s Despite a $60 barrier to entry, everything points towards the beta being huge. From the get go, the beta ran into problems due to sheer popularity, with WoW: Forever senior game producer Tom Ellis (who has since deleted their X account ) posting a technical breakdown that boiled many of the beta's initial issues down to the game's beta environment simply not being accustomed to such high demand. It wasn't long before other developers at Blizzard began to chime in on how unprecedented the Forever's beta seemed to be. WoW executive producer Holly Longdale posted that Forever's beta was "setting records." Two days later on September 19, she said "launch will be wild…and we are here for it, come what may." Most recently, Longdale chimed in about the beta's success once more. On September 27, she wrote Blizzard had to increase the beta's population cap once again. "The wild ride continues," she said . https://twitter.com/TheWindstalker/status/2104270224568541611?s=20 Longdale hasn't been the only one commenting on how big the beta seems to be. Senio

gamespot.com/articles/for-the-first-time.title: For The First Time Ever, Sony Skips CES, Which Was Home To One Of PlayStation’s Silliest Announcements
gamespot.com/articles/for-the-first-time.excerpt: Sony has attended every edition of the Consumer Electronics Show (CES) since it debuted in 1967 , but that's ending for the upcoming show in January 2027. This means there won't be any PlayStation news, at least not directly from Sony. The company confirmed to Bloomberg that it's pulling out of the show this year following a strategic evaluation of its approach to "events and communications based on the needs and priorities of our diverse business." The company went on to say that today it's putting more focus on "entertainment," including games, anime, films, and music. CES, on the other hand, is primarily a technology show. What PlayStation announcements have there been at CES before? Sony's showing at CES historically includes a keynote address, featuring executives and creative leaders from the company discussing upcoming technologies and products. Sony never made the most momentous PlayStation announcements at its CES events over the years, but it was an event that fans could expect some news, at least. For example, in 2020, then-PlayStation boss Jim Ryan revealed the PS5 logo at CES . At the time, people were clamoring for any morsel of news about the console, and fans roasted Sony for revealing only the logo. You can re-live the moment where everyone learned that the logo would be the most predictable logo ever in the video below. The juicier details like the release date, price, and technical specifics were saved for later events dedicated to the system. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E429XW4isFs At CES 2022, Sony unveiled PlayStation VR2 and a new game for it, Horizon: Call of the Mountain. In more recent years, Sony's PlayStation-related announcements at CES pertained to the company's transmedia adaptations, including the announcement of Horizon and Helldivers movies . Microsoft, for its part, revealed the original Xbox with Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson at CES 2001, but the company didn't carry the tradition forward with similarly big Xbox announcements at C

gamespot.com/articles/diablo-4-season-15.title: Diablo 4 Season 15 Is Filled To The Brim With Big Secrets, And They Just Keep Coming
gamespot.com/articles/diablo-4-season-15.excerpt: Diablo 4 Season 15 is stuffed full of secrets years in the making, and despite the season having launched two weeks ago, players keep discovering new ones. Season 15, Hell's Legacy, is a major nostalgia trip for Diablo fans. It adds new dungeons, boss fights, and items from previous Diablo games to Diablo 4, as players team up with Deckard Cain to defeat echoes of the Prime Evils and harness some of their iconic powers. But those references to previous games go far beyond a handful of dungeons and bosses. It also added a full Horadric Cube's worth of secrets. Some stem from older games in the franchise, while others are a continuation of ones added in Diablo 4 that players have worked towards uncovering for years. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9MabZDgAHLA After years of searching, Blizzard finally gave players the culmination of its secret cow-level hunt, as players who have gone through the laborious task of reaching the cow level and battling the cow king can now go even one step further to take on Moophisto , the Divine Bovine. In that same vein, players can also finally catch Mefishto , a secret fishing boss Blizzard went as far as to tease with a bizarre infomercial back when the game's Lord of Hatred expansion launched. Players were also quick to discover all kinds of new runewords and items from previous Diablo games, like the highly coveted Enigma that converts each class' evade into a teleport. But those are just some of the secrets. Players can also visit Old Tristram (complete with Diablo 1 NPCs like Griswold, Wirt and Adria) by finding all of Deckard Cain's journals, and even take on an Uber Prime Evil boss encounter there like in Diablo 2. For those who like their secrets silly, Diablo 3's Whimsyshire is now in the game after being teased as part of the cow-level quest, complete with hundreds of colorful killer teddy bears and unicorns. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q1QzrbZHR3g One of the coolest secrets in the seasons is the next phase of the Lucky

gamespot.com/articles/this-promising-new.title: This Promising New Soulslike Features A Black Metal Vocalist Among Its Impressive Cast
gamespot.com/articles/this-promising-new.excerpt: The main voice actor cast for upcoming soulslike Valor Mortis has been revealed, and its star-studded lineup features the surprising addition of a name better known for fronting a black metal band. Adam "Nergal" Darski will play the role of Captain Raphael. If his impressive growls and screams in Behemoth are anything to go by, players can expect a pretty dramatic rendition of the character. It's not his first rodeo, surprisingly. He also voiced The Black Cat in 2022's Blacktail and was the narrator for Apocalipsis: The Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil in 2018. https://youtu.be/JWD4BN8KUZ8 He's joining an impressive roster of voice actors, including Baldur's Gate 3 and Expedition 33's Jennifer English as The Shrike and Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Crimson Desert's James Alexander as William Dowsett. Napoleon Bonaparte will be played by Vincent Cassel, who has starred in the Ocean's Twelve and Ocean's Thirteen films as François Toulour. Mars Lipowski, who is best known for portraying Sobieslaw "Gromsko" Kosciuszko in the Call of Duty franchise, will take on the role of Lucjan Skawinski. Will De Renzy-Martin, who played Coen in The Blood of Dawnwalker, will portray James Stewart. Finally, Yvan Chamouiseau will step into the shoes of Louis Moreau. Valor Mortis is a first-person action soulslike from the developer of Ghostrunner. Set in an alternate 19th century Eastern Europe, Napoleon's endless war has led to a supernatural plague. You'll follow William, played by Alexander, as he fights to survive against his former comrades who are now undead monsters. Valor Mortis is set for release on Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and PC on October 13, and will be priced at $40 because this fall has a jam-packed release schedule, the developer admitted recently. It was originally scheduled for launch on September 24, but due to how busy September was , it was delayed by a few weeks.

gamespot.com/articles/behold-the-60-gear.title: Behold, The $60 Gears Of War Pizza Cutter That Looks Like A Real Pain In The Butt To Clean
gamespot.com/articles/behold-the-60-gear.excerpt: Xbox has announced its next collaboration, and it's a partnership with Prince St. Pizza for a specially branded Gears of War pizza and a $60 pizza-cutter. Microsoft and Prince St. Pizza teamed up to make a Prototype Lancer pizza-cutter to promote this October's Gears of War: E-Day, and it's available for $60 . To justify the steep price tag, Prince St. Pizza says it's a hefty metal cutter featuring a stainless steel blade and a handle that's meant to make you feel like you're wielding the iconic gun. The pizza-cutter also comes with the in-game pizza emblem. It does look pretty great, but it also looks like a real pain the butt to clean if you're a messy person like me. If anyone is wondering why it's called the Prototype Lancer and not just the Lancer, that's the special solution the developers came up with to explain why the heck a Lancer would even be in a prequel like E-Day . In the Gears of War lore, the weapon was created a year after the events of Emergence Day. However, you can't have a Gears game without the Lancer, so the developers called it a Prototype Lancer. Incredible. As for the pizza itself, it's called the Emergence Pie, and it's themed around this October's Gears of War: E-Day, which is a prequel that tells the story of Emergence Day. The pizza includes spicy vodka red sauce and mozzarella cheese, along with proteins in the form of pepperoni and sausage. The pizza is also doused with spicy Italian chili crisp. "Rugged, relentless, and built to hit hard, it’s the kind of pie that doesn’t go quietly," reads a line from Microsoft's blog post.  It's also a pizza that doesn't go quietly for your wallet, as it costs a mighty $46 before taxes or delivery fees if you're getting it sent to your home. The Gears of War pizza costs $46. The Emergence Pie is available now through November 1 at Prince St. Pizza locations in the US and Canada. gamespot.com/articles/steam-is-finally-c.title: Steam Is Finally Changing How Games Get Their Big Front-Page Break
gamespot.com/articles/steam-is-finally-c.excerpt: The front page of Steam has long been a hot commodity for game developers and publishers, but next year, some big changes are coming. Valve has announced that it'll be changing how it handles game discoverability during sales and promotions on Steam, as it'll be moving away from the old model of a tightly controlled page through a manually curated calendar to dynamic, personalized recommendations that'll cater to individual user preferences and their purchase history. Historically, Valve employees selected which games got featured in a limited number of fixed slots on the Steam front page, and only a fraction of discounted games got valuable front-page visibility. According to Valve, preliminary experiments resulted in up to 10 times as many games appearing per day in the Discounts & Events section, leading to measurable increases in store page visits and wishlist additions. Steam deals page What does this mean? For developers, it means that they won't need to rely on relationships, manual pitches, or sheer luck to potentially get a front-page placement. This will also effectively level the playing field for all developers, as smaller teams and publishers typically don't have the budget to compete with AAA blockbuster marketing teams. Valve added that it has already paused scheduling curated placements in the Weekend Deals, Midweek Deals, and Daily Deals sections, and it will soon roll out new and updated tools to help developers better manage their discounts and sale events on Steam. "Our goal is to let developers focus on crafting the most compelling games and deals for customers, and not spend time trying to convince someone at Valve to feature their products," Valve wrote . The rollout window for this change to the Steam storefront will be in early 2027. This news comes on the eve of a new Steam sales event, as the week-long Steam Autumn Sale kicks off on October 1. gamespot.com/articles/call-of-duty-modde.title: Call Of Duty Modders Add Skateboarding And Minecraft To Modern Warfare 2
gamespot.com/articles/call-of-duty-modde.excerpt: Modders have recently added new ways to play 2009's Modern Warfare 2, and videos are going viral, showcasing skateboarding in this classic Call of Duty game. Mechanics from games like Skate 2 were added with mods, and players can now kickflip and grind rails around their favorite Modern Warfare 2 maps. There's also a mod that puts Call of Duty players in Minecraft's sandbox world. As shown below in the video shared by " Chasm ," Call of Duty operators are seen pulling off several maneuvers on skateboards using game mechanics from Skate 2. These stunts include faceplanting on Rust, grinding rails on Terminal, and skating through the streets of Karachi. https://twitter.com/chasmmmmmmmmmmm/status/2104349115521888748 In addition to skateboarding, modders also included a Minecraft mod for Modern Warfare 2. As shown in the video shared by " Kiyy ," this modded version of MW2 loads the player into a Minecraft world with a custom loadout. This footage is shown as a Free-for-All game mode, and the player switches between various Modern Warfare 2 guns before decimating Minecraft pigs and sheep with the Spas-12 shotgun. https://twitter.com/KiyyDumb/status/2104657092359356464 It’s uncertain whether Activision will try to axe these mods, especially given the copyright issues involved, but both the Minecraft and Skate 2 mods are currently available on GitHub. It seems a theater mode mod is also in the works for Modern Warfare 2, allowing players to view and edit clips from their matches. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives on October 23, but in the meantime, players can try something different with mashups of Skate 2 and Minecraft. Modern Warfare 4 will release on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and PC. The game will include a full campaign, multiplayer, and the return of Infinity Ward's DMZ extraction mode.

gamespot.com/articles/xbox-ceo-insists-i.excerpt: The " Xbox reset " has people wondering whether Microsoft is preparing to exit the video game business, but Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has flatly denied that the gaming division will be put up for sale. "Xbox is not for sale," Sharma said to The New York Times . "We will do whatever it takes to set the company up for success, and we will look at the right partnerships, the right operating model, and everything needed to achieve that." Sharma's comments come in the wake of analysts predicting that Microsoft could sell Xbox off entirely . Compared with Microsoft's profitable cloud computing and artificial intelligence businesses, Xbox has paled in comparison, and the gamble on Xbox Game Pass hasn't paid off, despite Microsoft investing tens of billions in acquiring several video game publishers and studios over the years. Xbox’s accountability margins amount to only a 3% profit , a small return on investment for its parent company. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XiYNNGR4uLo Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has said that Xbox will have to start pulling its weight under Sharma's leadership, and the Xbox CEO previously told employees that the Xbox business was not in a healthy state. Nadella has also praised Sharma's cuts at Xbox, saying they have led to a "streamlining" of the division . If Sharma is setting Xbox up to generate more profit for Microsoft, then it's all part of a years-long strategy in the making. Halo is now an Activision project, and is likely several years away as the publisher is currently building a new team to develop the next Master Chief adventure. Meanwhile, two of Blizzard's biggest upcoming games will arrive at the end of this decade: Diablo 5 is aiming for a 2029 launch , while StarCraft is set for 2030 . At the same time, Xbox has also tasked several of its studios with working on its Fallout franchise, with multiple new games in the series in various stages of development. gamespot.com/articles/you-can-hate-the-s.title: You Can Hate The Sonic Movies, But They Help The Games Get Made, Sega Says
gamespot.com/articles/you-can-hate-the-s.excerpt: Sonic has had a rough go at things lately, what with the myriad games that haven't been hitting like they used to. Sega appears to be aware of that and has acknowledged that, although the games have struggled recently, the franchise as a whole is back in the zeitgeist again--and it's all thanks to the live-action movies. In an interview with Automaton at the Tokyo Game Show , series producer Takashi Iizuka spoke about the impact that director  Jeff Fowler's three live-action movies have had on repopularizing Sonic again. "Thanks to the movies, awareness of the Sonic series has grown, and more people around the world have become interested in Sonic as a character and in the games," Iizuka said when asked about the positive effect other media has had on the franchise. "That has contributed to game sales as well. Strong game sales mean we have more resources available when making the next title, which allows us to deliver something of even higher quality. That creates a positive cycle. In that sense, multimedia and transmedia expansion are majorly beneficial for the games." Iizuka went on to say that movies weren't the only medium that has improved Sonic the Hedgehog's cachet in recent times. Anime has contributed as well, and so has Netflix, which has made film and television production more ubiquitous for Sega. "In the past, even if we decided to make an anime as part of our transmedia strategy, we had to approach television broadcasters and other outlets that would air it, and we couldn't move forward without their approval," Iizuka continued. "With Netflix, on the other hand, once we decide to work together on something, we can distribute it worldwide. That's has [sic] been a major advantage when it comes to expanding the brand." Iizuka's comments echoed similar sentiments from earlier this month. In an interview with One More Game on September 21 , Iizuka said the live-action movies essentially saved the franchise. gamespot.com/articles/wow-forever-is-kee.title: WoW: Forever Is Keeping More Than 12,500 Items Secret
gamespot.com/articles/wow-forever-is-kee.excerpt: World of Warcraft: Forever is looking to keep its secrets, as over 12,500 items in the game's files have been kept hidden from dataminers. The WoW: Forever beta is currently in full swing, and in addition to new dungeons, abilities, and even a whole new playable race, players are quickly discovering there are tons of new items that will completely change how this old-school version of WoW is played. Whether it's items with far more spellpower at early levels or gear tailored towards professions, Blizzard is definitely mixing things up so that the game's leveling journey, and its endgame, are going to feel all new. As broken down in detail by Icy Veins , part of how Blizzard looks to be accomplishing this is by keeping almost 40% of the game's nearly 32,000 items a secret. Dataminers can technically see that these 12,000 plus items exist and even where many of them potentially come from, but can't see what their stats are. Many of these items are assumed to be all-new, though some are likely variants or modified version of items from WoW Classic. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dvueCoFTkCk&t Players have already taken a bite out of that 12,500 item total, having discovered over 4,400 "hidden" items in the Forever beta. Once an item has been discovered, it's then revealed in the game's backend. Icy Veins notes that not all the items datamined might actually exist in Forever, as it lists a number of items that were part of WoW Classic's Season of Discovery and might not make it into Blizzard's new version of the MMO. Many of the hidden items come from raids and dungeons, including tier sets. So far, players have uncovered a few different sets, such as some low-level dungeon item sets, as well as full loot tables for early-game dungeons like Wailing Caverns, Ragefire Chasm, Shadowfang Keep, and the Deadmines. The beta's level cap is currently 20 (but will be raised to 30 before the beta's end), meaning players will likely uncover even more dungeon loot ahead of launch.

gamespot.com/articles/yes-guile-street-f.title: Yes, Guile’s Street Fighter Movie Theme Goes With Everything
gamespot.com/articles/yes-guile-street-f.excerpt: The Street Fighter movie is shaping up to be a love letter to Capcom's classic fighting game series, with its goofy action and costumes, but if there's one crucial element it's nailing, it's the franchise's sound. Specifically, Guile's iconic theme, which is legendary for its ability to complement anything in life. How does the movie version match up? It's not straying from what is considered fighting game soundtrack perfection, but it is adding to it with a kickass guitar solo and a few more cinematic tweaks, allowing the main theme to do all the heavy lifting. Listen to it yourself, from one of the streaming links below: Apple Music Spotify Amazon Music YouTube Music Deezer Tidal Guile's Theme is one of those evergreen memes of the late 2000s and early 2010s, and while it's nowhere near as popular as it once was--YouTube probably got sick of all those 10-hour uploads--it's still instantly recognizable. The original theme debuted in the 1991 arcade release of Street Fighter II and was composed by Yoko Shimomura. For the upcoming Street Fighter movie, the score was produced by Leo Birenberg and Zach Robinson (Cobra Kai), who say that the original game soundtracks were instrumental in shaping their musical identities. "As young and budding composers, we listened to Yoko Shimomura's iconic Guile’s Theme probably more than Raiders of the Lost Ark," the duo said in a press statement. "We hope fans will hear the love and reverence we hold for this music within our version of Guile’s Theme. https://youtu.be/U6sbm1OaJb8 The full Street Fighter soundtrack will feature 39 tracks in total, and it'll be available starting October 16. The movie releases on the same day, and so far it looks like it's leaning fully into the absurdity of its source material. WWE performer Cody Rhodes plays Guile , and if you feel like cosplaying as him, you can grab an official Street Fighter popcorn bucket shaped like his iconic hair. Absolutely perfect, no notes. CD Projekt Red detailed the patch on social media , stating that the team is working on another hotfix for PC that will address a save game issue that numerous players have reported. The bloom setting doesn't fix everything though. Players have still taken issue with the game's HDR implementation, path tracing visual presentation, and overall system performance on PC. CD Projekt Red hasn't yet commented on whether it is planning to make changes to those areas, but this patch does indicate that they are aware of the most glaring issues players are facing. gamespot.com/articles/your-debt-is-paid-.title: Your Debt Is Paid Turns Your Worst Financial Nightmare Into A Roguelike
gamespot.com/articles/your-debt-is-paid-.excerpt: Money can't buy you happiness, but it can buy you a reprieve from nightmarish bosses lurking inside a dark dungeon. That's the idea behind Your Debt Is Paid, a new fantasy-themed roguelike auto-battler from developer Cmski. Originally made in two weeks for the Creepy Clicker Horror Game Jam 2026, Cmski's idea has been expanded for this full release on PC via Steam. After the protagonist is captured by a mysterious being and dumped into a monster-filled dungeon, they strike a cruel bargain with their captor: Pay an ever-growing blood debt to secure their freedom, or forfeit their life in this roguelike experience. Designed to resemble a '90s "forgotten cartridge" game, Your Debt Is Paid mixes retro visuals with dark fantasy, as players experiment with build combinations to create the ultimate warrior. Every expedition is a gamble, but with some cunning and luck, you can transform your cursed adventurer into a one-hit-kill machine. Defeating monsters will reward you with Blood currency, which you can then spend to gain more strength or pay off your debt. Just how far do you want to push your luck? That's up to you, as the more you play, the more heroes, bloodlines, realms, and Ascension Levels you'll unlock along the way, allowing you to form new strategies on the fly. The game is designed to be easy to learn, and since battles unfold automatically, you can take all the time you need to make crucial decisions to guarantee your survival. Your Debt Is Paid will be coming to PC in early 2027. That's going to be a bit of a wait for Your Debt Is Paid, but if you want to check out an auto-battler that puts a unique spin on the growing genre, Blood Dungeon comes highly recommended. It's essentially a Survivors-like for people who don't like Survivors-likes , as it offers both automatic and acrobatic combat, with a focus on platforming.

gamespot.com/reviews/gears-of-war-e-days.title: Gears Of War: E-Day’s Campaign Is Buried In The Past
gamespot.com/reviews/gears-of-war-e-days.excerpt: The best prequels typically share the same thing in common. Whether it's Red Dead Redemption 2, Yakuza 0, Metal Gear Solid 3, or Halo: Reach, each game tells a story that recontextualizes what came before. Revisiting a game after playing its prequel should alter the experience, providing you with new knowledge that changes how you perceive certain characters, places, and scenes. The events of Red Dead Redemption 2 add emotional weight to the first game and John Marston's mission by humanizing his targets, just as Yakuza 0 deepens the bond between Kazuma Kiryu and Akira Nishikiyama, making the first game's tragic finale much more impactful. Gears of War: E-Day doesn't do anything like this. The Coalition's latest venture back to the world of COGs and Locusts is a prequel to the 2006 original with nothing new to say. You already know where it's going: protagonists Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago go to war as the human world of the surface is invaded by the subterranean Locust, and the heroes survive to fight another day. Even then, there aren't any surprises on the way there. The most notable changes occur within the framework of its third-person, cover-based shooting. It's still distinctly Gears of War--full of meaty men wielding crunchy weapons--just with a few new bells and whistles added to improve aspects of its signature action. It's good, and the increased spectacle is impressive, but it doesn't do enough to elevate to greatness. For a series that has struggled, or been unwilling, to let go of the past, purposefully going back 14 years prior to the surprise attack that incited the series at least sounded like a solid idea. By tackling the past head-on, with one of the most important days in the series' fictional history, The Coalition gave itself the chance to examine the origins of Marcus, Dom, and the antagonistic Locust Horde from the very moment their fates intertwined. gamespot.com/articles/how-long-is-gears-.title: How Long Is Gears of War: E-Day – Mission List And Hours Played
gamespot.com/articles/how-long-is-gears-.excerpt: Gears of War: E-Day is almost here--unless you're hopping in a few days early with the Premium Edition--and if you're looking to try out the campaign, you can settle in for a few days of action and chainsaw executions. While Gears of War: E-Day is primarily a linear cover-based shooter, the game also sprinkles in some semi-open-world environments for you to explore between missions, giving you the opportunity to hunt down collectibles, upgrades, and take part in side missions. Here’s how long it’ll take you to beat Gears of War: E-Day. How long to beat Gears of War: E-Day depending on your play style If you tackle the Gears of War: E-Day campaign on normal difficulty, do a little bit of collectibles hunting and take part in the game's non-story missions, expect the campaign to take 10-14 hours to complete. In my own playthrough, I motored through the campaign and finished it in 11 hours, occasionally stopping along the way to track down a hidden item, find an upgrade pack for my arsenal, and take part in a side quest. I'd done roughly 60% of that content before I reached the end, and Gears of War: E-Day has a war journal that provides a very comprehensive list of things you missed in each mission, so you can go back and find them for a completionist run. That's a fairly standard playthrough time for a game in this series, and once you've rolled credits, the various multiplayer modes look like they'll consume plenty of your hours. You can increase the difficulty and spend more time in the campaign, but on higher challenge levels, enemies can be bullet-sponges that quickly burn through your stock of spare lives. Horde Siege looks like an especially enjoyable timesink, as this new take on the Gears of War horde mode revolves around three teams of four players taking on waves of enemies, co-operating with each other to accomplish objectives, and survive against increasingly overwhelming odds. gamespot.com/articles/ubisofts-massive-e.excerpt: After folding several of its studios into " Creative Houses " earlier this year, Ubisoft has announced a rebranding for Creative House 2, which might be slightly confusing. The branch that is home to almost all of Ubisoft's Tom Clancy-branded games, Creative House 2 will now be known as Massive Entertainment, which is also the name of one of Ubisoft's longest-serving studios. Massive Entertainment, as a studio, will still exist within Massive Entertainment the Creative House, and this arm of Ubisoft will continue to grow existing IP and work on new projects, like the upcoming March of Giants. "Starting today, development teams responsible for these franchises in Montréal, Paris, Sweden, and Toronto will operate under the Massive Entertainment brand, bringing together their creative and technology expertise to shape its future, grow these franchises and craft challenging experiences for dedicated player communities," Ubisoft said in a statement. Even the logo is massive. Massive Entertainment--the studio--was established in 1997 in Sweden, and it was acquired in 2002 by Vivendi. After Activision and Vivendi merged in 2008, the developer was sold to Ubisoft and has remained with the publisher ever since. The developer has been a hitmaker for Ubisoft, assisting Ubisoft Montreal on major titles such as Assassin's Creed Revelations and Far Cry 3, while also developing two entries in The Division series. Its most recent release was the divisive Star Wars Outlaws in 2024, and the studio is currently working on The Division 3 . This rebranding follows in the footsteps of Creative House 1, which is known as Vantage Studios. rockpapershotgun.com/capcom-arent-just-r.title: Capcom aren't just running out of Resident Evil games to remake - they're banking on it, with a mysterious "crossover" planned when the timelines collide
rockpapershotgun.com/capcom-arent-just-r.excerpt: Capcom have done a brisk trade in Resident Evil remakes this past decade. They've gone back to formula with Resident Evil 2 , Resident Evil 3 , and Resident Evil 4 , not just bumping up the resolution and revarnishing the cutscenes, but writing new variations on the old survival horror fables. There's a Resident Evil: Code Veronica regurgitation due in 2027, and a Resident Evil 0 resurrection allegedly to follow in 2028 . The problems with this strategy are perhaps expressed by my previous sentence's struggle to come up with extra synonyms for "remake": sooner or later, Capcom are going to run out of original games they can credibly overhaul. Including the forthcoming or rumoured projects, they've only got Resident Evils 5 and 6 left now before they hit the "modern era" inaugurated by Resident Evil 7, the game that introduced the fancy RE Engine used by the remakes. The truth is that, outside of showing off the setting and a few of the characters Gerry'll chat to, they've kept their lips pretty tight. rockpapershotgun.com/we-want-people-to-t.title: "We want people to try and outsmart the game": No Law aims for Arkane-style reactivity within a dangerous walled city
rockpapershotgun.com/we-want-people-to-t.excerpt: Port Desire, the hemmed-in city setting of immersive sim No Law, is hard to place. At points, it reminds me of walking around Lisbon. It shares that Portuguese city's verticality, where hill-straddling streets shouldered by colourful houses and corner shops can feel like tiers on a wedding cake. The strong sunlight and bursts of foliage reinforce the mediterranean vibes. Yet, the port city's structure and history is much closer to Kowloon Walled City, the ungoverned Chinese enclave that existed within British-owned Hong Kong. Through the 1900s, with the British government taking a hands-off policy to the tiny district and the Chinese government exercising no control over its citizens, Kowloon became the most densely populated city on earth, with 33,000 citizens living in just 2.6-hectare borders. With virtually no official police presence, the city attracted anyone looking for a less-observed, less-regulated life – gangs, refugees, and a surprising number of unlicensed dentists. As one of No Law's creative directors, Tor Frick, tells it, Port Desire is very similar. Not specifically the dentists bit, more the general, isolated lawlessness. Read more

Players buying gold from third-party websites that use bots to farm the game's primary currency has been a problem for the entirety of WoW's existence and has always been against the game's terms of service. What's changed is that developer Blizzard has made comments that it's looking to more aggressively punish gold buyers in Forever, even going as far to admit its been too "lenient" on the matter in the past. That more hardline stance against gold buyers was put to the test earlier this week when WoW: Forever streamer Ziqo was seen on stream accepting suspiciously large amounts of gold from strangers in the lead-up to a $100,000 prize pool PvP tournament he and many other streamers will be competing in. In a forum post seemingly issued in response to the Ziqo controversy, Blizzard stated that it would increasingly punish not only gold sellers, its standard practice, but also those buying the gold. In addition, accounts accepting large amounts of questionable gold could also be punished by having the illicit gold removed, their account suspended, or even permanently banned. Blizzard encouraged players not to accept "suspicious" transactions to avoid these consequences. gamespot.com/articles/the-street-fighter.title: The Street Fighter Movie’s Most Obscure Easter Egg Is For True Fighting Game Nerds
gamespot.com/articles/the-street-fighter.excerpt: Ahead of its release later this month, marketing for the Street Fighter movie has focused on deep references to the long-running fighting game series. How deep? We already knew that fighting game legend Justin Wong--alongside Michael "IFC Yipes" Mendoza--was making a cameo as one of the inmates who watches Ryu take on Blanka in a prison fight , but even his prisoner costume hides one heck of an Easter egg. Any fighting game fan will instantly recognize it: on Wong's neck, you can spot the number 37, a reference to the legendary Evo Moment 37 . In a new behind-the-scenes video, Wong detailed the time he spent on the Street Fighter movie set getting fake dirt and dressing up for his cameo. If you're unfamiliar with the significance of the fake 37 tattoo his character sports, it's a deep-cut nod to what many consider one of the greatest fighting game comebacks in history. Back in 2004, Wong faced off against Daigo Umehara, and with his chosen brawler, Chun-Li, down to just a sliver of health and backed into a corner, Wong parried over a dozen attacks from Umehara's Ken Masters and found the perfect window to counter the onslaught. https://youtu.be/ssipFrggf58 It's a moment that has yet to be equaled within the fighting game community, with the clip earning an obscene number of views over the decades. This is just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the accuracy the Street Fighter movie is aiming for, as the film embraces the unique look of the Capcom games with its choice of costumes, special attacks, and goofy hairstyles that double as the perfect popcorn bucket . Chun-Li actress Callina Liang even went the extra mile to get into fighting shape for the movie, focusing on conditioning her thighs to look impressively muscular and memorizing Chun-Li's various attacks. gamespot.com/reviews/i-cannot-believe-si.title: I Can’t Believe A Silly Star Wars Racing Roguelite Is One Of My Favorite Games This Year
gamespot.com/reviews/i-cannot-believe-si.excerpt: I felt such a sense of whiplash jumping into Star Wars Galactic Racer after playing Zero Company . Unlike Zero Company--and plenty of the other Star Wars games we've gotten in recent years, like Survivor and Squadrons --Galactic Racer isn't trying to emulate the science-fantasy drama that defines the majority of the Star Wars movies and other assorted fiction. Instead, it's silly. We're not making morally gray decisions in a fight against an evil empire here. No, we're trying to win a racing league in order to dethrone the comically evil rich competitor mounting some kind of hostile takeover of the league. Oh, and we have an infinite number of chances to qualify, and protagonist Shade can walk away from the most violent of wrecks without a scratch. It's such a ludicrous situation that makes no sense if you think through the logistics of it for even a moment. And yet that very absurdity is exactly what racing in the Star Wars universe is all about. It sees competitors strapping themselves into barely functioning death machines to jockey against each other at breakneck speeds while soaring past lava, through narrow desert canyons, over acid-filled valleys, and alongside icy cliffs to the cheers and jeers of a bloodthirsty audience. Everything about the competition is comically ridiculous, and by leaning into that irrationality, Galactic Racer not only feels authentic to that fantasy, but it's also a hilariously good time. You race through the game as Shade, a former-racer-turned-cargo-pilot, who finds themselves brought back into the sport as both a favor to the league's commissioner and as a means of seeking revenge against Kestar Bool, an arrogant champion who wronged Shade in the past. Galactic Racer doesn't do too much to set up the stakes for this plot, framing Shade's revenge through a lens of a mystery. What did Kestar do to Shade? Why does Shade always wear a helmet? gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-should-blaze.title: GTA 6 Should “Blaze A Trail” To More Expensive Games, Dev Says
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-should-blaze.excerpt: Rockstar's GTA 6 is priced at $80 for its standard edition. Another voice has come forward to say they hope other teams follow suit and charge more for new games to help the industry at a time when developers are closing up shop, cancelling games, and laying off developers on a regular basis. Martin Klima, the co-founder of Kingdom Come developer Warhorse, told PC Gamer that raising unit prices would "help a lot," but "everybody's scared to death" to do it. "Now, hopefully, GTA will blaze the trail, and it will allow us to increase the cost," he said, adding that Rockstar and Take-Two are among the only companies who can "afford, or who can dare" to raise prices in this way. He added that price increases for new games are "long overdue and also necessary for this business to survive." GTA 6 should kick off a trend of games costing more, Warhorse co-founder says. Take-Two was among the first big publishers to drive prices up from $60 to $70, kicking this off with NBA 2K21 in 2020. Numerous other publishers followed suit, and now $70 is the norm. Defending the price increase, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said production costs increased by 300%. Former PlayStation executive Shawn Layden said in 2025 that the price of new games should have gone up with every new console generation for the past 20 years. That largely did not happen, and now the industry is worse off for it, he said. “I think it’s because everyone’s afraid,” he told GI.biz . “No one wants to be the first one to raise the price, because you’re afraid to lose traffic. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-takes-the-ri.title: GTA 6 Takes The Ridiculous World We Live In And Turns It Up To 11
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-takes-the-ri.excerpt: Video games are usually a few steps removed from reality, but with Grand Theft Auto 6 , developer Rockstar Games aims to reflect and amplify the current state of the world with an "over the top" experience. As seen in the trailers and gameplay previews so far, GTA 6 is a contemporary game about doing whatever it takes to make it to the top, and that pursuit of fame and glory is often bookended by shootouts, car chases, and explosions in its Bonnie and Clyde narrative. "If you are going to put all this effort into creating a version of today’s world, it has to be more over the top, more insane, more in your face," senior VP of narrative Rupert Humphries said to Love Magazine . "Otherwise, you could just go outside and live in the real world." Humphries also described the world of GTA 6 as "a pressure cooker for all kinds of insanity," as the protagonists, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, are polar opposites. Game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern described Lucina as an ambitious go-getter who'll do anything to get the life she dreams of, while Jason is bound by life's circumstances. "We wanted both protagonists to be vulnerable, tough, flawed, right sometimes, wrong sometimes, able to learn from each other," Gauvey-Kern said. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_vlzIPpyJR0 GTA 6 is also making some big changes to the franchise formula, as getting out of trouble won't be as easy as hiding in an alley and waiting for your wanted level to drop. Actions have consequences, and with the cops being much smarter and more persistent, players will have to be more cunning before they embark on a crime spree. The relationship between Jason and Lucia is also surprisingly more nuanced and deeper than you think, and it'll be a major part of the overall GTA 6 experience when the game launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. rockpapershotgun.com/desktop-and-handhel.excerpt: I don’t know if memory shortages have permanently killed off the concept of 'cheap' gaming PCs, but they have at least beat it into a coma. On the desktop side, inflated RAM, SSDs and graphics card prices continue to inflict karmic pain for our years of "It's cheaper to build it yourself" smugness, while formerly affordable handheld PCs are either suffering 40%-plus jackups or launching above £1K from the off. And the Steam Machine ! The poor, square Steam Machine . Every few weeks, possibly in denial, I’ll skim through the shops to see what budget games kit actually looks like in this day and age. Across the last five or six rounds, little has changed: the entry point into decent, more-or-less current-spec 1080p play remains stuck in the low quadruple figures, particularly if you’re fully new to PC ownership and need to factor in a monitor and peripherals. There is one exception, assuming you don’t fancy your luck on the secondhand market , but giving it a hands-on appraisal means confronting an ancient hardware foe of mine. Xbox is adding these all the time, but we wanted to draw your attention to three particularly big examples that have all landed on the Xbox Store over the past couple of days. The first of these is the demo for Castlevania: Belmont's Curse , which allows you to start the game and carry over your progress to the full release later in October. The second one is a FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves demo, which follows the well-received launch of the full game earlier this year, and the final one is a demo for Elta: Defy All Gods , which features 60 minutes of gameplay from the upcoming action-platformer, with the demo already boasting a highly "Positive" reception on Steam. Read the full article on purexbox.com

purexbox.com/news/2026/10/despite-how-am.title: Despite How Amazing Xbox Disc To Digital Is, There's Some Sadness Around Forza Horizon
purexbox.com/news/2026/10/despite-how-am.excerpt: It's not really a surprise though. We've seen a lot of people really enjoying the new Xbox Disc to Digital feature ever since it rolled out for everyone earlier this week, and as mentioned previously, it supports over 1,500 physical games with potentially more to come. That means there are obviously some games that don't work though, and if there's one request we're seeing more than anything else, it's for Xbox to somehow find a way to gain support for various Forza Horizon games. Read the full article on purexbox.com
